events.title: Hong Kong Stock Market Due For Support
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, sinking almost 900 points or 3.8 percent in that span. The Hang Seng now sits just above the 22,400-point plateau although it may halt its slide on Monday.

events.title: Steady Start Eyes For China Stock Market
events.description: The China stock market has moved lower in two straight sessions, sliding more than 50 points or 1.4 percent along the way. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just above the 3,530-point plateau although it may find traction on Monday.

events.title: Taiwan Stock Market May Find Traction On Monday
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has finished brutally lower in back-to-back sessions, plummeting more than 4,150 points or 10.3 percent in that span. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 36,030-point plateau and it's due for support on Monday.

events.title: Bargain Hunting May Boost Singapore Stock Market
events.description: The Singapore stock market headed south again on Friday, one day after ending the five-day losing streak in which it had tumbled more than 225 points or 4.5 percent. The Straits Times Index now sits just above the 4,975-point plateau although it may tick higher again on Monday.

events.title: Little Movement Expected For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has tracked lower in four straight sessions, sinking more than 30 points or 1.9 percent along the way. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just above the 1,555-point plateau although it's looking at a steady start on Monday.

events.title: Tech Shares May Continue To Weigh On KOSPI
events.description: The South Korea stock market on Friday ended the two-day winning streak in which it had rallied almost 170 points or 3.4 percent. The KOSPI now sits just beneath the 4,870-point plateau and it may take further damage on Monday.

events.title: Australia Manufacturing PMI Sinks To 48.7 In November - S&P Global
events.description: The manufacturing sector in Australia continued to contract in November, and at a faster pace, the latest survey from S&P Global revealed on Monday with a manufacturing PMI score of 48.7.

events.title: New Zealand Retail Sales Climb 2.2% In Q3
events.description: The volume of retail sales in New Zealand was up a seasonally adjusted 2.2 percent on quarter in the third quarter of 2026, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday - coming at NZ$26 billion.

events.title: Singapore Inflation Data Due On Monday
events.description: Singapore will on Monday release October figures for consumer prices, highlighting a light day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Ends Roughly Flat Amid Rising Expectations On Fed Tightening
events.description: The U.S. Dollar value ended almost flat on Friday after several U.S. Federal Reserve officials concurred on the need to raise the interest rates in the December meeting while the U.S.-Iran stalemate continues with no resolution in sight.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Weak For 4th Straight Session
events.description: The Switzerland market ended weak on Friday, extending recent losses, as rising uncertainty about AI trade and rising cost of debts, as well as fears of possible interest rate hikes by central banks rendered the mood bearish.

events.title: European Markets Close Notably Lower As AI Trade Concerns Trigger Sell-off
events.description: European stocks fell on Friday and several markets across the region hit multi-week lows - some markets even dropped to multi-month lows - weighed down by losses in several sectors, especially in the technology space amid uncertainty about the sustainability of AI trade despite Anthropic's historic IPO.

events.title: TSX Sinks To 6-Month Low As Tech Sector Crumbles
events.description: Canadian equities tumbled Friday as technology stocks plunged 4.4% following global AI trade concerns. The benchmark index dropped 418.25 points to 33,610.48. Materials and financial sectors also declined significantly on weak commodity prices.
